title: Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment
summary: SAME characterized aerosols from four overheated spacecraft materials and a dibutyl-phthalate reference in ISS microgravity using heating below ignition and controlled smoke aging. The 47 flight-log records cover 30 initial sample tests and 17 reheats; they are smoke-generation measurements, not flammability-limit tests.

tests.notes: Flight log: GMT 252 (2007 flight campaign), source Sample Type = Silicone, Reheat/Initial = Initial, carousel 1, position 1. Record Time in source: 11:50 - 13:20. This recording interval is not a measured heating or burning duration. Flow velocity not specified for this run in the flight log; left null. The CSV summary does not map its 5/10 cm/s conditions to these flight Test Numbers, so those values were not assigned. O2 = 21% and pressure = 101.3 kPa assumed from nominal ISS cabin conditions per docs/data-extraction.md; not reported measurements for this run. Outcome no_ignition is an interpreted mapping of the below-ignition-temperature heating protocol (Abstract, PDF p. 3). No ignition challenge or flammability pass/fail is reported; aerosol generation does not establish fire resistance. Flow direction, specimen thickness, burn length and flame spread rate are not reported for this run and remain null. The approximate cylinder diameter in the apparatus description is not treated as specimen thickness. Ground aerosol comparisons do not provide a corresponding burn outcome; normal_gravity_reference remains null.
